{{1973 Iowa Conference football standings}}
The '''1973 Buena Vista Beavers football team''' was an [[American football]] team that represented [[Buena Vista College]] as a member of the Iowa Conference (now known as the [[American Rivers Conference]]) during the [[1973 NAIA Division II football season]]. In their fourth year under head coach [[Jim Hershberger]], the Beavers compiled an 8–1 record (7–0 in conference games), won the Iowa Conference championship, and outscored opponents by a total of 208 to 106.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1974 |title=1974 Buena Vista University Yearbook |page=18|url=https://www.iowaheritage.org/files/original/8edccda7eeea3d432265bc4a97ba0068.pdf |access-date=July 15, 2024 |website=Iowa Heritage}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Final Iowa Conference football standings |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/42043901/globegazette/ |newspaper=[[Globe Gazette]] |location=[[Mason City, Iowa]] |date=November 14, 1973 |page=25 |access-date=January 10, 2020 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] {{Open access}} }}</ref> The team's only loss was to the eventual NAIA Division II national champion [[1973 Northwestern Red Raiders football team|Northwestern Red Raiders]].<ref name=buenor>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=99-Yard March Aids Raiders |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-des-moines-register/133027963/ |newspaper=[[The Des Moines Register]] |location=[[Des Moines, Iowa]] |date=September 23, 1973 |page=7D |access-date=October 6, 2023 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] {{Open access}} }}</ref> It was Buena Vista's first outright conference championship since 1952.<ref>{{cite news|title='Ho-Hum' Beavers Just 7-0|newspaper=Des Moines Register|date=November 12, 1973 |page=4S|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-des-moines-register-ho-hum-beavers/152852235/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

Guard Joe Kotal was selected as a first-team All-American. Quarterback Charlie Mullligan was selected as the Iowa Conference Most Valuable Player, and Hershberger received the conference's Coach of the Year award.

The team played its home games at Bradford Field in [[Storm Lake, Iowa]].

==Awards and honors==
Buena Vista personnel received multiple honors at the end of the 1973 season, including the following:

* Guard Joe Kotval, a 6-foot-3, 250-pound senior, was selected by the [[Associated Press]] (AP) as a first-team player on the [[1973 Little All-America college football team]]. It was Kotval's second consecutive year winning All-America honors.<ref>{{cite news|title=Buena Vista Guard Honored: Iowan Kotval All-American|newspaper=Des Moines Tribune|date=December 6, 1973|page=1S|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/des-moines-tribune-buena-vista-guard-hon/152853820/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Two Coe Gridders Cited|newspaper=The Cedar Rapids Gazette|date=December 7, 1973|page=17|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-gazette-two-coe-gridders-cited/152854117/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>
* Senior quarterback Charlie Mulligan, who passed for 907 yards and six touchdowns, was unanimously selected as the Most Valuable Player in the Iowa Conference.<ref name=BVQ/>
* Head coach Jim Hershberger was selected as the Iowa Conference Coach of the Year.<ref name=BVQ/>

In addition to Mulligan and Kotval, six other Buena Vista players were selected as first-team players on the 1973 All-Iowa Conference football team: tight end Steve McPherson; interior offensive lineman Lyle Karsten; defensive linemen Tom Rouse and Kent Livermore; linebacker Tom McGrain; and defensive back Mike Pertzborn.<ref name=BVQ>{{cite news|title=Buena Vista Quarterback Top Player|newspaper=The Cedar Rapids Gazette|date=November 20, 1973|page=15|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-gazette-buena-vista-quarterback-top/152852685/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref name=BVH>{{cite news|title=Buena Vista Heads Iowa Loop 'Stars'|newspaper=Des Moines Register|date=November 21, 1973|page=3S|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-des-moines-register-buena-vista-head/152853274/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>
